data.name: Ojal
data.short_meaning: Goddess Ojaswini, symbolizing strength and vitality
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Ojas’, which means ‘vital energy’ or ‘strength’, Ojal is a feminine name inspired by the Goddess Ojaswini. This divine figure is revered for her power and vitality, often invoked to strengthen the body and mind. In Hindu mythology, Ojaswini is also associated with wisdom and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Ojal was a legendary king of the Haihayas in the 11th or 12th century CE in the central Indian region of Malwa. He is mentioned in the Prabandha Khanda of the 13th-century work Hari-Bhagavata Purana.
historical_references.context: Legendary king of the Haihayas in central Indian region of Malwa

historical_references.reference: Ojal is also mentioned in the 15th-century work Adipurana, which is the first epic of the Jaina tradition in the Prakrit language. He is described as a powerful king of the Malava country and a devotee of Mahavira.
historical_references.context: Powerful king of Malava country and a devotee of Mahavira in Jaina tradition

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ojal: The name Ojal is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Oj' which means vital energy or life force. 'Al' in the name signifies 'Aatma' or the soul.
